doc: Every creature the game defines: enemies, wildlife, farm animals and villagers: their level, faction, size, health and damage scaling, resistances, speeds, random loot and the enemy's sight. An edit is global: every creature of the entry, now or later, as the field says.

ids.rule: A creature has the id of its template: the template's debug name in lower case (Enemy_Vukah_Melee is game:enemy_vukah_melee). A template without a name is game:template_<first 8 hex digits of its GUID>. When two templates would get the same name, the one that held it first keeps it and the other is game:<name>~<first 8 hex digits of its GUID>. The entries are the templates with an enemy's, a wild animal's, a farm animal's or a villager's behaviour; the same id names the template in every registry.

traits.animal: a farm animal or pet (kind animal)
traits.villager: a villager or workshop NPC (kind villager)

kind.doc: What the creature is, by the behaviour it has: an enemy, a wild animal, a farm animal or pet, a villager.

level.doc: The level a creature spawns at when its spawner sets none (most spawners set their own). Creatures that spawn after the edit get it; creatures already in the world keep the value they spawned with.

levelMax.doc: The highest level the creature can have; a level above it is cut to it. Creatures that spawn after the edit get it; creatures already in the world keep the value they spawned with.

faction.doc: The side the creature fights for (playerAlly: on the players' side). Creatures that spawn after the edit get it; creatures already in the world keep the value they spawned with.

scale.doc: The creature's size (1 = as made). Only a creature that has a size value of its own can take one. Creatures that spawn after the edit get it; creatures already in the world keep the value they spawned with.

xp.doc: The factor on the experience a kill gives (1 = as the game gives). Creatures that spawn after the edit get it; creatures already in the world keep the value they spawned with.

health.doc: How the creature's health grows. Health itself comes from its level through the game's formulas.

levelFactor.doc: The factor of the health a level adds (the game's level scaling). Read at the creature's next health update.

perPlayer.doc: The health added per player nearby beyond the first, as a share (0.48 = 48 %). Read at the creature's next health update.

multiplier.doc: The factor on all the damage the creature deals (1 = as made). Creatures that spawn after the edit get it; creatures already in the world keep the value they spawned with.

perPlayer.doc: The damage added per player nearby beyond the first, as a share (0.05 = 5 %). Read at the creature's next health update.

resist.doc: How much of each kind of damage the creature takes: 1 = normal, 0 = immune, 2 = double. Creatures that spawn after the edit get it; creatures already in the world keep the value they spawned with.

physical.doc: The share of physical damage as a whole the creature takes.

cut.doc: The share of cutting damage the creature takes.

pierce.doc: The share of piercing damage the creature takes.

blunt.doc: The share of blunt damage the creature takes.

wood.doc: The share of wood damage (tools) the creature takes.

stone.doc: The share of stone damage (tools) the creature takes.

metal.doc: The share of metal damage (tools) the creature takes.

poison.doc: The share of poison damage the creature takes.

explosion.doc: The share of explosion damage the creature takes.

skillShot.doc: The share of skill-shot hits (weak spots) the creature takes.

fire.doc: The share of fire damage the creature takes.

shroud.doc: The share of shroud damage the creature takes.

ice.doc: The share of ice damage the creature takes.

lightning.doc: The share of lightning damage the creature takes.

speed.doc: How fast the creature moves, in metres per second. Creatures that spawn after the edit get it; creatures already in the world keep the value they spawned with.

combat.doc: Its speed when moving in combat.

loot.doc: The random loot a killed creature leaves. Creatures that spawn after the edit get it; creatures already in the world keep the value they spawned with.

disabled.doc: The creature leaves no random loot.

slots.doc: How many random loot rolls a kill gives: a number from min to max.

arsenal.doc: The enemy's arsenal: the attacks it chooses from (arsenals registry). Creatures of the same kind share one.

sight.doc: What an enemy sees. Read at once by every enemy of the entry, also those already in the world.

range.doc: How far the enemy sees a target by day, in metres (night shortens it by the game's night factor).

engageRange.doc: Within this distance, in metres, the enemy engages a target it sees at once.
